quotes.text: If your failover requires a manual meeting or a functioning control plane during a blackout, you do not have a plan. You have hope.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Captures the episode's central warning in two sentences.

quotes.text: The reality is simple. Multi-region deployment doesn't make you resilient. Your state strategy does. In the old model, architects treated databases like black boxes.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes resilience around data rather than deployment locations.

quotes.text: Resilience means having the capacity reserved before the rest of the world tries to buy it. Your recovery should be a pushbutton event that only requires a routing change.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A concrete recommendation against redeploy-on-demand recovery plans.

quotes.text: There is no phone call, there is no slack thread, the telemetry is the only authority that matters.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarizes the case for automated, telemetry-driven failover decisions.

quotes.text: You have to break things on purpose to make sure they don't break on their own. This level of rigor is what separates the architects who build systems from the ones who just build hopes.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A memorable argument for regular failure testing.

takeaways: Global edge services and DNS are dependencies that need regional bypass paths, not invisible utilities.
Recovery plans that depend on redeploying through the control plane fail when everyone hits the same management APIs and capacity runs out, so pre-provision warm standbys.
Resilience comes from a deliberate state strategy, automated failover governance and regular chaos testing.
hook: Deploying to two Azure regions does not make a system resilient if failover depends on a meeting, a healthy control plane or capacity you never reserved. This episode walks cloud architects through edge, DNS, control plane, data and governance failures in a regional outage and shows how to design systems that keep running.
